lessons.title: Equipment from lairage to bleeding
lessons.html:
Know your equipment

A small stock slaughterer uses many tools and machines. You must know what each one is for, how to use it safely, how to check it and how to clean it. Only use equipment you have been trained and authorised to use.

Lairage and moving animals

  • Pens, races and gates to hold and move sheep and goats.
  • Water troughs in every pen.
  • Flags, paddles or rattles to guide animals without hurting them.

Restraining and stunning

  • Restrainer: a V-shaped conveyor or a stunning pen that holds the animal still.
  • Electrical stunner (tongs): the tongs are placed on the head so current passes through the brain. Settings are fixed by the plant. Check cables and tongs before use.
  • Captive bolt pistol: fires a bolt into the head to stun. Used for some goats, rams with heavy horns, or as a back-up. It uses cartridges or compressed air. Load it only when ready to use, always point it at the ground when not in use, and store it locked.

Hoisting and bleeding

  • Shackles: chains or hooks for the hind leg.
  • Hoist: lifts the stunned animal onto the bleeding rail.
  • Bleeding trough: collects blood.
  • Sticking knife: a sharp, pointed knife for cutting the blood vessels in the neck.

Before each shift, check that the stunner works, the back-up stunner is ready, and the hoist and shackles are in good condition. Report any fault at once.

lessons.title: Knives, saws and dressing equipment
lessons.html:
Knives

KnifeUse
Sticking knifeBleeding
Skinning knife (curved, rounded tip)Opening and freeing the skin without cutting it
Boning or general knifeRemoving feet, head, evisceration, trimming

Keeping knives sharp

  • Use a steel often during the shift to keep the edge straight.
  • Knives are sharpened on a stone or machine by a trained person.
  • A sharp knife is a safe knife. Blunt knives slip.
  • Carry knives in a scabbard, never in your hand while walking.

Other dressing equipment

  • Hock cutters or shears: cut off the feet.
  • Overhead rail, hooks, gambrels and spreaders: hold the carcass while it is dressed.
  • Hide puller in some plants: a machine that pulls the skin off.
  • Brisket saw or cutter: opens the breastbone if needed.
  • Offal trays, chutes and hooks: hold the guts and organs, matched to the carcass.
  • Work platforms: let workers stand at the right height.

Safety with powered equipment

  • Use only if trained and authorised.
  • Check guards and emergency stops before use.
  • Keep hands away from blades and moving parts.
  • Switch off and lock out before cleaning or clearing a blockage.
  • Report damaged cables, guards and hoses.

lessons.title: Hygiene and protective equipment
lessons.html:
Hygiene equipment

  • Knife sterilizers: boxes of very hot water at each station. Put your knife in after each carcass and whenever it touches something dirty. Report a sterilizer that is not hot.
  • Hand-wash basins: knee-, foot- or sensor-operated taps so that clean hands do not touch dirty taps. Must have soap and paper towels.
  • Apron wash and boot wash stations.
  • Hoses for cleaning, used with care so water does not splash onto carcasses.

Chilling and weighing equipment

  • Scale on the rail to weigh carcasses. It must be checked (calibrated) so weights are correct.
  • Chillers with thermometers or temperature displays.
  • Marking equipment: inspection stamps and classification roller marks, used only by authorised people.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)

  • Overall or coat, waterproof apron, hairnet
  • White rubber boots with non-slip soles
  • Cut-resistant glove and, where provided, a chain-mail apron or arm guard
  • Hearing protection near noisy machines
  • Warm clothing for the chillers
  • Gloves and goggles for cleaning chemicals

Caring for equipment

  1. Check before use.
  2. Use correctly.
  3. Clean and sanitise after use as the cleaning schedule says.
  4. Store in the right place.
  5. Report damage. Never use broken equipment.

Key points

  • Use only equipment you are trained and authorised to use.
  • Check the stunner and back-up stunner before each shift.
  • Keep knives sharp with a steel, and carry them in a scabbard.
  • Sterilise knives in hot water after each carcass.
  • Lock out machines before cleaning.
  • Wear your PPE every shift.
